title: Asset vs Borrowed Liquidity Management and the Investment Function
august: Asset liquidity management and borrowed liquidity management.

maps.tested: Rated Very Important with no crash-course coverage available, but absent from every exam recall in this dataset.
maps.specifics: Investment instruments available to banks, the factors affecting the choice of securities, tax-exposure considerations, and reserve-management strategy. Rated high by the provider; unconfirmed by candidate reports.

vardeezReading: LTR-5: Moderate. "LO 70.a and LO 70.b". LTR-4: Very Important. "Money market investments; LO 69.c apply investment maturity strategies".

selectors.name: Asset vs borrowed vs balanced liquidity
selectors.what: Compares asset liquidity management (asset conversion), borrowed liquidity management (liability management) and the balanced strategy: the pros, cons, risk, instruments and who uses which. Asset conversion is the less risky approach, used mainly by smaller institutions; borrowed liquidity is the riskiest with the highest expected return, used most by the largest banks.

selectors.name: Net liquidity position as the starting point
selectors.what: Net liquidity position Lt = supplies (deposit inflows, nondeposit service revenues, loan repayments, asset sales, money market borrowings) - demands (withdrawals, acceptable loan requests, repaid borrowings, operating expenses, dividends). L < 0 is a deficit, L > 0 a surplus; also the factors that drive supply and demand of liquidity.
selectors.theory: Why supply rarely equals demand, why a firm is liquid only with access to immediately spendable funds at reasonable cost at the right time, the liquidity versus profitability trade-off, and why depositories face liquidity problems (maturity mismatch, demandable liabilities, rate sensitivity, public confidence).

selectors.name: Investment instruments for banks and trade-offs
selectors.what: The money market instruments (T-bills, agency securities, CDs, Eurocurrency deposits, bankers' acceptances, commercial paper, short-term municipals) and capital market instruments (Treasury, municipal, corporate and asset-backed securities) with the advantages and disadvantages of each.

selectors.name: Factors in choosing securities, tax exposure
selectors.what: The factors affecting the choice of investment securities: expected return, tax exposure, interest rate, credit, business, liquidity, call, prepayment and inflation risk, and pledging requirements. Tax part: after-tax yield = before-tax yield x (1 - t); tax-equivalent yield = tax-exempt yield / (1 - t).
selectors.theory: Why tax-exempt municipals suit a taxpaying bank, why TEY divides and after-tax yield multiplies by (1 - t), and the distinctions between call and prepayment risk and between business and credit risk.

selectors.name: Investment maturity strategies and tools
selectors.what: Maturity strategies (ladder, front-end load, back-end load, barbell, rate expectations) and the yield-curve and duration tools used to manage maturity, including immunisation by setting duration equal to the planned holding period.
